facts.fact: Founded in 1893 on its present site in Oak Bay; the oldest 18-hole course in Canada in its original location. Began as 14 holes, 18 by 1895; the layout played today was settled in the mid-1920s.
facts.source: https://www.victoriagolf.com/ (home page, read 2026-10-31 through the fetch workflow, release data-victoria club_home.html)

facts.fact: The course sits on a rocky point at the south-east tip of Vancouver Island, overlooking the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
Oak Bay is named for its Garry oaks (Quercus garryana); the Olympic Mountains of Washington stand across the strait, south of the course (interpretation of the setting, standard geography).
The club's own crest is not used or imitated (interpretation).

concepts.name: The Garry Oak on the Point
concepts.rationale: The two things every round at Victoria shows: the Garry oaks on the rock outcrops, and the Olympic Mountains across the strait.
concepts.symbolism: Oak for Oak Bay, rock for the point, mountains for the view south.
concepts.interpretation: A composed scene, not a particular tree.
concepts.strengths: Says where it is: an oak, a rock and the mountains across the water. Reads at 32 px.
concepts.tradeoffs: A scene rather than one object; the mountains are small at 1x.

recommendation: Concept 1 (the only concept; a new course).
